content.text: Single audit provision found (§ 4.4), binding Corio (our client).

input.quote: Such books and records shall be kept for at least three (3) years following the end of the calendar month to which they pertain, and shall be open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio for the purpose of verifying the amounts payable to Commerce One under this Agreement. Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit/inspection right running against Corio (the customer/licensee here). It matches the preferred position on the material terms: frequency is capped at once per calendar year; inspections are limited to reasonable times and upon reasonable notice; the audit must be performed by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio (better than a mere independence requirement, and Corio holds a veto); Commerce One bears all audit costs unless the inspection reveals an underpayment exceeding 5%, which is the preferred cost-shifting threshold; and there is no right of access to Corio systems — review is limited to books and records, with no remote or direct access language anywhere in the document. The only sub-element short of the preferred wording is that notice is expressed as "reasonable notice" rather than a fixed 30 (or 15) days' written notice; that is a minor drafting gap rather than a material failure, since the clause is neither unlimited nor unannounced, and we would not spend negotiating capital on it. Noted for information only; no redline proposed.
